walkthrough.gettingStarted.title: Get Started with Singular Blockly
walkthrough.gettingStarted.description: Build your first Arduino, CyberBrick, or TXT Controller program with blocks and upload it to your board.
walkthrough.gettingStarted.openEditor.ti: Open the editor and choose a board
walkthrough.gettingStarted.openEditor.de:
Open a writable folder first; your blocks are saved in it. Then click the Singular Blockly icon in the activity bar and pick your board from **Select Board**.
[Open Blockly Editor](command:singular-blockly.openBlocklyEdit)
walkthrough.gettingStarted.openEditor.al: Opening the Blockly editor from the activity bar and selecting Arduino Uno.
Drag blocks and watch the code

Drag blocks from the toolbox into **Setup** and **Loop**, then change values with the dropdowns. Keep the generated file (for example `src/main.cpp`) open beside the editor to see the program update as you work.
Building a blink program by dragging blocks while src/main.cpp updates next to the editor.
walkthrough.gettingStarted.upload.title: Upload to your board
walkthrough.gettingStarted.upload.descri:
Connect your board and click **Upload** in the editor toolbar. Arduino boards upload through PlatformIO, CyberBrick through USB or paired Wi-Fi, and the TXT Controller through SSH. If an Arduino upload fails, check PlatformIO first.
[Check PlatformIO Status](command:singular-blockly.checkPlatformioStatus)
walkthrough.gettingStarted.upload.altTex: The Upload button in the Blockly editor toolbar.
walkthrough.gettingStarted.personalize.d:
Expand the toolbar with the arrow button, use the globe menu to change the editor language, and use the theme button to switch between light and dark. Stuck or have an idea? Tell us without a GitHub account.
[Provide Feedback](command:singular-blockly.provideFeedback)
walkthrough.gettingStarted.personalize.a: Switching the editor to Traditional Chinese and the dark theme.
